server/discover.instructions:
Example Helpdesk holds the Example company's support tickets. Ticket IDs look like T-1042, and dates are in UTC.

- To find a ticket, use search_tickets, then get_ticket with its ID. Don't guess IDs.
- update_ticket changes only the fields you send. Before changing the status or assignee of a ticket the person didn't mention, ask them.
- delete_ticket can't be undone. Only use it when the person asks to delete a specific ticket; otherwise set its status to closed.
- For questions about workload or trends, use ticket_volume_chart.
- helpdesk://guides/getting-started explains what each status and priority means.

tools.title: Search tickets
tools.description: Finds tickets by words in their subject and messages, most recently updated first. Use it to find a ticket before reading or changing it. limit.description: How many tickets to return at most.

tools.name: get_ticket
tools.title: Get a ticket
tools.description: Gets one ticket in full: subject, status, priority, requester, assignee, tags, dates and its address in the web app. Use it when you know the ticket's ID, from search_tickets or from the person; it doesn't search.

id.description: The ticket's ID: T- and a number.

assignee.description: Who's working on it. Absent while it's unassigned.

tools.name: update_ticket
tools.title: Update a ticket
tools.description: Changes a ticket's status, priority, assignee or tags. Fields you leave out stay as they are, and sending the same values again changes nothing. Send at least one field besides id.

id.description: The ticket's ID: T- and a number.

assignee.description: Who to assign it to, by email address.

tags.description: The ticket's tags, replacing the ones it has: lowercase words and dashes.

tools.name: delete_ticket
tools.title: Delete a ticket
tools.description: Deletes a ticket and its messages for good. Only use it when the person asks to delete that ticket; to stop work on one, set its status to closed with update_ticket instead.

id.description: The ticket's ID: T- and a number.

reason.description: Why it's being deleted, kept in the audit log.

tools.name: ticket_volume_chart

tools.description: Charts how many tickets came in over the last days, one bar per status or priority, as a PNG image with a one-line summary. Use it for questions about workload and trends.

tools.description: Fetches an article from the public help center at help.example.com, as Markdown. Use it to quote or summarize published help for a requester. It only fetches help.example.com addresses.

# When a printer shows offline

1. Check that the printer is on and its screen shows no error.
2. Print a configuration page from the printer's menu, and check that its IP address starts with 10.3.
3. On your computer, remove the printer and add it again from Settings, then Printers.

Still offline? Open a ticket and include the configuration page.

contents.text:
# Getting started with Example Helpdesk

Every ticket has an ID like T-1042, a subject, a status and a priority.

## Statuses

- **open**: someone needs to act on it.
- **pending**: waiting for the requester to answer.
- **solved**: fixed. It closes by itself after 7 days.
- **closed**: done for good. A closed ticket can't be reopened; open a new one instead.

## Priorities

low, normal, high and urgent. An urgent ticket pages whoever is on call, so only raise a ticket to urgent when the requester can't work at all.

content.text: Summarize this ticket for the support team in three short paragraphs: the problem, what has been tried, and the next step. Keep the requester's own words where you can.
List the open tickets from most to least urgent. For each, say in one line why it's urgent and who should take it, from the people already working on similar tickets.
I'll search the open tickets first, then read the urgent and high-priority ones in full before ordering them.
